questions.explanation: Multiply the fractions: 2/3 x 3/4 = 6/12, which simplifies to 1/2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Work out 2/3 of 3/4.

questions.explanation: Multiply the fractions: 3/5 x 2/7 = 6/35, which is already in its simplest form. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Work out 3/5 of 2/7.

questions.explanation: Loss = 60 - 48 = £12. Percentage loss = (loss / cost price) x 100 = (12/60) x 100 = 20%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A shop buys a lamp for £60 and sells it for £48. What is the percentage loss?

questions.explanation: Loss = 150 - 126 = £24. Percentage loss = (24/150) x 100 = 16%. A common mistake is dividing the loss by the selling price instead of the cost price. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A trader buys a bike for £150 and sells it for £126. What is the percentage loss?

questions.explanation: Comparing digit by digit after the decimal point: 0.399 is smallest, then 0.4 (=0.400), then 0.45 (=0.450), then 0.454. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Order from smallest to largest: 0.45, 0.4, 0.454, 0.399.

questions.explanation: Comparing the tenths digit first: 0.09 and 0.099 both have 0 tenths, which is less than the others. Comparing 0.09 (=0.090) and 0.099, 0.09 is smaller. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Which of these is the smallest: 0.09, 0.9, 0.099, 0.19, 0.9099?

questions.explanation: Dividing 5 by 8 gives 0.625. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Convert 5/8 to a decimal.

questions.explanation: Dividing 7 by 16 gives 0.4375. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Convert 7/16 to a decimal.

questions.explanation: Multiplication first: 1/4 x 2/3 = 2/12 = 1/6. Then add: 1/2 + 1/6 = 3/6 + 1/6 = 4/6, which simplifies to 2/3. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Work out 1/2 + 1/4 x 2/3.

questions.explanation: Multiplication first: 1/2 x 1/3 = 1/6. Then subtract: 3/4 - 1/6 = 9/12 - 2/12 = 7/12. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Work out 3/4 minus 1/2 x 1/3.

questions.explanation: If 2/5 was spent, 3/5 remains, which equals £54. So 1/5 = 54/3 = £18, and the total (5/5) = 18 x 5 = £90. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: After spending 2/5 of his money, Tom has £54 left. How much money did he start with?

questions.explanation: If 3/8 was given away, 5/8 remains, which equals 30 sweets. So 1/8 = 30/5 = 6, and the total (8/8) = 6 x 8 = 48. A common mistake is treating the 30 remaining sweets as 3/8 of the total instead of 5/8. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: After giving away 3/8 of her sweets, Priya has 30 sweets left. How many sweets did she start with?

questions.explanation: 0.75, 75% and 6/8 are all equivalent to 3/4. 3/5 equals 0.6, which is different. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT equal to 3/4: 0.75, 75%, 6/8, 3/5?

questions.explanation: 0.4, 40%, 4/10 and 8/20 are all equivalent to 2/5. 5/2 equals 2.5, which is very different (it's the reciprocal, not an equivalent form). (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Which of these is NOT equal to 2/5?

questions.explanation: The ratio parts add up to 3+7=10. The first part is 3 out of 10, which as a percentage is (3/10) x 100 = 30%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Express the first part of the ratio 3:7 as a percentage of the whole.

questions.explanation: The ratio parts add up to 2+3=5. Boys make up 2 out of 5, which as a percentage is (2/5) x 100 = 40%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: In a class, the ratio of boys to girls is 2:3. What percentage of the class are boys?

questions.explanation: A 15% decrease leaves 100%-15%=85% of the original, which as a multiplier (decimal) is 0.85. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: What single multiplier represents a 15% decrease?

questions.explanation: An 8% increase gives 100%+8%=108% of the original, which as a multiplier (decimal) is 1.08. A common mistake is using just 0.08, which represents the increase alone, not the new total. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: What single multiplier represents an 8% increase?

questions.explanation: Discount: 3/10 of £20 = £6, so the sale price is £20-£6=£14. Booking fee: 5% of £14 = £0.70. Total: £14+£0.70=£14.70. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A book costs £20. Maya buys it in a sale with 3/10 off, then pays an extra 5% booking fee on the sale price. How much does she pay in total?

questions.explanation: Discount: 1/5 of £45 = £9, so the discounted price is £45-£9=£36. Service charge: 10% of £36 = £3.60. Total: £36+£3.60=£39.60. A common mistake is applying the service charge to the original £45 instead of the discounted price. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A meal costs £45. A 1/5 discount is applied, then a 10% service charge is added to the discounted price. What is the final price?

questions.explanation: Increase: 200 x 1.1 = £220. Decrease: 220 x 0.9 = £198. Notice this is NOT back to £200 - a common misconception is assuming a % increase followed by the same % decrease cancels out exactly. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A price of £200 increases by 10%, then decreases by 10%. What is the final price?

questions.explanation: Decrease: 150 x 0.8 = £120. Increase: 120 x 1.2 = £144. A common mistake is assuming the two changes cancel out and giving £150. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A price of £150 decreases by 20%, then increases by 20%. What is the final price?

questions.explanation: If 3/4 of the number is 24, then 1/4 of the number is 24/3=8, so the whole number is 8x4=32. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: 3/4 of a number is 24. What is the number?

questions.explanation: If 2/5 of the number is 18, then 1/5 of the number is 18/2=9, so the whole number is 9x5=45. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: 2/5 of a number is 18. What is the number?

questions.explanation: Increase = 52-40=12cm. Percentage increase = (increase / original) x 100 = (12/40) x 100 = 30%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A plant grows from 40cm to 52cm. What is the percentage increase?

questions.explanation: Decrease = 80-68=£12. Percentage decrease = (12/80) x 100 = 15%. A common mistake is dividing by the new value instead of the original value. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A price drops from £80 to £68. What is the percentage decrease?

questions.explanation: 20% of 150 = 30. 15% of 180 = 27. Since 30 is greater than 27, '20% of 150' is the larger amount. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Which is greater: 20% of 150, or 15% of 180?

questions.explanation: 35% of 80 = 28. 25% of 120 = 30. Since 30 is greater than 28, '25% of 120' is the larger amount. A common mistake is comparing just the percentages (35 vs 25) without calculating the actual amounts. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Which is greater: 35% of 80, or 25% of 120?

questions.explanation: Interest per year = 5% of 200 = £10. Over 3 years (simple interest is the same each year): 10 x 3 = £30. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Sam invests £200 at 5% simple interest per year. How much interest will he earn after 3 years?

questions.explanation: Interest per year = 4% of 500 = £20. Over 2 years: 20 x 2 = £40. A common mistake is compounding the interest (adding interest onto interest) instead of using simple interest, which stays constant each year. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Priya invests £500 at 4% simple interest per year. How much interest will she earn after 2 years?

questions.explanation: 1 3/4 = 1.75 as a decimal. Converting to a percentage: 1.75 x 100 = 175%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Convert 1 3/4 to a percentage.

questions.explanation: 2 1/5 = 2.2 as a decimal. Converting to a percentage: 2.2 x 100 = 220%. A common mistake is only converting the fractional part and forgetting the whole number, giving 20%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Convert 2 1/5 to a percentage.

questions.explanation: After Monday, 2/3 remains. On Tuesday, 1/4 of that remaining 2/3 is used: 1/4 x 2/3 = 1/6 of the original. Remaining after Tuesday: 2/3 - 1/6 = 4/6 - 1/6 = 3/6 = 1/2. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A tank starts full. 1/3 of the water is used on Monday. Then 1/4 of the remaining water is used on Tuesday. What fraction of the original tank is left?

questions.explanation: After day 1, 4/5 remains. On day 2, 1/2 of that remaining 4/5 is eaten: 1/2 x 4/5 = 2/5 of the original. Remaining: 4/5 - 2/5 = 2/5. A common mistake is treating the fractions as if they combine directly (1/5 + 1/2) rather than applying the second fraction to what remains. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A cake starts whole. 1/5 is eaten on day 1. Then 1/2 of what's left is eaten on day 2. What fraction of the original cake remains?

questions.explanation: Offer A: each item costs 40 x 0.7 = £28, so two items cost 2 x 28 = £56. Offer B: full price (£40) plus half price (£20) = £60. Offer A gives the lower total. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A £40 item has two offers: Offer A gives 30% off each item. Offer B is 'buy one, get the second half price'. If you buy TWO items, which offer gives the lower total cost?

questions.explanation: Offer A: each item costs 60 x 0.8 = £48, so two items cost 2 x 48 = £96. Offer B: full price (£60) plus half price (£30) = £90. Offer B gives the lower total. A common mistake is assuming a percentage discount is always better without calculating both totals. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A £60 item has two offers: Offer A gives 20% off each item. Offer B is 'buy one, get the second half price'. If you buy TWO items, which offer gives the lower total cost?

options.text: Offer A, because 20% sounds bigger than half

questions.explanation: Percentage = (15/60) x 100 = 25%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: 15 out of 60 students walk to school. What percentage of students walk to school?

questions.explanation: Percentage = (42/120) x 100 = 35%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: 42 out of 120 tickets sold were for children. What percentage of tickets sold were for children?

questions.explanation: Discount: 1/5 of 150 = £30, so the sale price is 150-30=£120. VAT: 20% of 120 = £24. Final price: 120+24=£144. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A £150 washing machine has 1/5 taken off in a sale. VAT of 20% is then added to the sale price. What is the final price?

questions.explanation: First discount: 80 x 0.85 = £68. Loyalty discount: 68 x 3/4 = £51. A common mistake is applying both discounts to the original price separately instead of applying the second discount to the already-reduced price. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: An £80 jacket has 15% taken off. Then a further 1/4 discount is applied to the reduced price for loyalty members. What does a loyalty member pay?

questions.explanation: 1 = 8/8. Subtracting: 8/8 - 3/8 = 5/8. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Work out 1 minus 3/8.

questions.explanation: Convert to twelfths: 1 = 12/12, 1/3 = 4/12, 1/4 = 3/12. Subtracting: 12/12 - 4/12 - 3/12 = 5/12. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Work out 1 minus 1/3 minus 1/4.

questions.explanation: Cross multiply: 5x10=50 and 7x7=49. Since 50 is greater than 49, 5/7 is the bigger fraction. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Using cross multiplication, determine which is bigger: 5/7 or 7/10.

questions.explanation: Cross multiply: 4x11=44 and 5x9=45. Since 45 is greater than 44, 5/11 is the bigger fraction. A common mistake is comparing the numerators or denominators directly instead of cross multiplying. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Using cross multiplication, determine which is bigger: 4/9 or 5/11.

questions.explanation: Rent, food and travel add up to 40+25+20=85%, so savings is 100-85=15%. Savings amount: 2,000 x 0.15 = £300. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A family's monthly budget of £2,000 is split as: 40% rent, 25% food, 20% travel, and the rest savings. How much do they save each month?

questions.explanation: Transport, accommodation and food add up to 35+30+20=85%, so activities is 100-85=15%. Amount: 5,000 x 0.15 = £750. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A school's £5,000 trip budget is split: 35% transport, 30% accommodation, 20% food, and the rest activities. How much is spent on activities?

questions.explanation: An hour has 60 minutes. 3/4 of 60 = 45 minutes. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: What is 3/4 of an hour, in minutes?

questions.explanation: An hour has 60 minutes. 5/6 of 60 = 50 minutes. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: What is 5/6 of an hour, in minutes?

questions.explanation: Year 1: 20,000 x 0.9 = £18,000. Year 2: 18,000 x 0.9 = £16,200. A common mistake is subtracting 20% (2x10%) from the original value directly, giving £16,000 instead. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A car worth £20,000 loses 10% of its value each year. What is it worth after 2 years?

questions.explanation: Year 1: 8,000 x 0.95 = £7,600. Year 2: 7,600 x 0.95 = £7,220. A common mistake is calculating 10% off the original value in one step, giving £7,200. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A machine worth £8,000 loses 5% of its value each year. What is it worth after 2 years?

questions.explanation: Convert to eighths: 3/4 = 6/8. Difference: 6/8 - 5/8 = 1/8 mile. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Tom ran 3/4 of a mile. Ben ran 5/8 of a mile. How much further did Tom run than Ben, as a fraction of a mile?

questions.explanation: Convert to tenths: 2/5 = 4/10. Difference: 7/10 - 4/10 = 3/10 litre. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A jug contains 7/10 of a litre. A bottle contains 2/5 of a litre. How much more is in the jug than the bottle?

questions.explanation: 12.5% = 12.5/100 = 125/1000. Simplifying by dividing both by 125: 125/1000 = 1/8. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Convert 12.5% to a fraction in its simplest form.

questions.explanation: 37.5% = 37.5/100 = 375/1000. Simplifying by dividing both by 125: 375/1000 = 3/8. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Convert 37.5% to a fraction in its simplest form.

questions.explanation: 3/4 of 600 = 450g. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A recipe serves 8 people and uses 600g of flour. How much flour is needed to make 3/4 of the recipe?

questions.explanation: 2/3 of 480 = 320ml. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A recipe uses 480ml of milk to serve 12 people. How much milk is needed to make 2/3 of the recipe?

questions.explanation: 0.7 = 70%. Since 70% is greater than 65%, 0.7 is bigger. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Which is bigger: 0.7 or 65%?

questions.explanation: 0.3 = 30%. Since 35% is greater than 30%, 35% is bigger. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Which is bigger: 0.3 or 35%?

questions.explanation: 18/40 simplifies by dividing both by 2: 18/40 = 9/20. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: In a survey, 18 out of 40 people preferred tea over coffee. Give this as a fraction in its simplest form.

questions.explanation: 15/25 = 0.6 as a decimal. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: In a class of 25, 15 students play a musical instrument. Give this as a decimal.

questions.explanation: 3/5 x 20 = (3 x 20) / 5 = 60/5 = 12. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Work out 3/5 multiplied by 20.

questions.explanation: 5/8 x 32 = (5 x 32) / 8 = 160/8 = 20. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Work out 5/8 multiplied by 32.

questions.explanation: 15% of 3.60 = 3.60 x 0.15 = £0.54. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Find 15% of £3.60.

questions.explanation: 25% of 7.60 = 7.60 x 0.25 = £1.90. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Find 25% of £7.60.

questions.explanation: When fractions share the same numerator, the one with the smaller denominator is bigger (the whole is divided into fewer, larger pieces). Since 5 is less than 8, 3/5 is bigger than 3/8. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Which is bigger: 3/8 or 3/5?

questions.explanation: When fractions share the same numerator, the one with the larger denominator is smaller. Since 9 is greater than 6, 5/9 is smaller than 5/6. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Which is smaller: 5/6 or 5/9?

questions.explanation: 3/8 means 3 parts out of 8 total. The remainder is 8-3=5 parts, giving the ratio 3:5. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Express the fraction 3/8 as a ratio of the part to the remainder.

questions.explanation: 2/7 means 2 parts out of 7 total. The remainder is 7-2=5 parts, giving the ratio 2:5. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Express the fraction 2/7 as a ratio of the part to the remainder.

questions.explanation: 1/4 = 0.25 as a decimal. Adding: 0.25 + 0.35 = 0.6. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Work out 1/4 + 0.35. Give your answer as a decimal.

questions.explanation: 3/5 = 0.6 as a decimal. Subtracting: 0.6 - 0.15 = 0.45. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Work out 3/5 minus 0.15. Give your answer as a decimal.

questions.explanation: The VAT-inclusive price is 120% of the original: original x 1.2 = 60, so original = 60 / 1.2 = £50. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A price of £60 includes 20% VAT. What was the price before VAT was added?

questions.explanation: The VAT-inclusive price is 120% of the original: original x 1.2 = 138, so original = 138 / 1.2 = £115. A common mistake is subtracting 20% of £138 directly instead of dividing by 1.2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A price of £138 includes 20% VAT. What was the price before VAT?

questions.explanation: 3 out of 5 is the fraction 3/5. As a decimal, 3/5=0.6. As a percentage, 0.6 x 100 = 60%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: 3 out of 5 students walk to school. Express this as a fraction, a decimal, and a percentage.

questions.explanation: 7/20 as a decimal is 0.35 (7 divided by 20). As a percentage, 0.35 x 100 = 35%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: 7 out of 20 tickets were discounted. Which of these correctly shows this as a fraction, decimal, and percentage?

questions.explanation: 20% of 50 = £10 saved. 15% of 80 = £12 saved. Since £12 is more than £10, the 15% off the £80 item saves more money, even though 15% is a smaller percentage. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Which saves more money: 20% off a £50 item, or 15% off an £80 item?

questions.explanation: 10% of 200 = £20 saved. 25% of 70 = £17.50 saved. Since £20 is more than £17.50, the 10% off the £200 item saves more money. A common mistake is assuming the larger percentage always saves more without checking the actual amounts. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Which saves more money: 10% off a £200 item, or 25% off a £70 item?

options.text: 25% off the £70 item, because 25% is a bigger percentage

questions.explanation: Maya's age = 2/3 of 24 = 16. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Maya is 2/3 of her sister's age. If her sister is 24, how old is Maya?

questions.explanation: Leo's age = 3/4 of 32 = 24. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Leo is 3/4 of his brother's age. If his brother is 32, how old is Leo?

questions.explanation: 47.85 / 4 = 11.9625, which rounds to £11.96 to the nearest penny. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bill of £47.85 is split equally between 4 people. How much does each person pay, rounded to the nearest penny?

questions.explanation: 68.20 / 3 = 22.7333..., which rounds to £22.73 to the nearest penny. A common mistake is rounding to £22.74 or truncating instead of rounding correctly. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A bill of £68.20 is split equally between 3 people. How much does each person pay, rounded to the nearest penny?

questions.explanation: Cara read 11 books and Ben read 5 books. Difference: 11 - 5 = 6. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows the number of books read by 4 students: Amy 8, Ben 5, Cara 11, Dan 6. How many more books did Cara read than Ben?

questions.explanation: Comparing all four values, £620 (Shop B) is the highest. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows sales for 4 shops: Shop A £450, Shop B £620, Shop C £380, Shop D £510. Which shop had the highest sales?

options.text: Shop A and B are equal

questions.explanation: Each symbol represents 4 pets, so 3 symbols represent 3 x 4 = 12 dogs. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A pictogram shows the number of pets owned by a class, where each symbol represents 4 pets. The row for dogs shows 3 symbols. How many dogs are there?

questions.explanation: Each symbol represents 10 items, so 4.5 symbols represent 4.5 x 10 = 45 apples. A common mistake is rounding the half-symbol up or down instead of using it as exactly half the value. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A pictogram shows fruit sales, where each symbol represents 10 items. The apple row shows 4.5 symbols. How many apples were sold?

questions.explanation: The rises between each hour are: 9-10am +2, 10-11am +3, 11am-12pm +2, 12pm-1pm -1 (a fall). The biggest rise, +3 degrees, was between 10am and 11am. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A line graph shows the temperature over 5 hours: 9am 4C, 10am 6C, 11am 9C, 12pm 11C, 1pm 10C. Between which two consecutive hours did the temperature rise the most?

questions.explanation: Total growth from Week 1 to Week 4: 14-5=9cm, over 3 growth intervals (Week1 to 2, 2 to 3, 3 to 4). Average growth per week: 9/3=3cm. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A line graph shows a plant's height over 4 weeks: Week 1 5cm, Week 2 9cm, Week 3 12cm, Week 4 14cm. What was the average weekly growth over the 4 weeks?

questions.explanation: 25% is equivalent to the fraction 1/4. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A pie chart shows how a class travels to school: Walk 50%, Bus 25%, Car 15%, Bike 10%. What fraction of the class travels by bus?

questions.explanation: A full pie chart is 360 degrees. Banana's share as a percentage: (180/360) x 100 = 50%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A pie chart shows favourite fruits: Apple 90 degrees, Banana 180 degrees, Orange 54 degrees, Other 36 degrees. What percentage of people chose Banana?

questions.explanation: 40% of 200 = 200 x 0.4 = 80 people. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A pie chart shows that 40% of 200 survey respondents prefer tea. How many people prefer tea?

questions.explanation: The sector's fraction of the whole: 90/360=1/4. Number of students: 240 x 1/4 = 60. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A pie chart shows a sector of 90 degrees out of 360 degrees represents students who play football, out of a total of 240 students. How many students play football?

questions.explanation: Adding all the values: 34+28+19+12 = 93. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A table shows ice cream sales by flavour: Vanilla 34, Chocolate 28, Strawberry 19, Mint 12. What is the total number of ice creams sold?

questions.explanation: Comparing all four values, 48mm (February) is the lowest. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A table shows rainfall (mm) for 4 months: January 65, February 48, March 72, April 55. Which month had the least rainfall?

questions.explanation: The highest is Q4 (71) and the lowest is Q1 (45). Difference: 71-45=26. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A table shows the number of cars sold each quarter: Q1 45, Q2 62, Q3 58, Q4 71. What is the difference between the highest and lowest quarterly sales?

questions.explanation: Total expenses: 450+280+120+150=£1,000. Food's percentage: (280/1000) x 100 = 28%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A table shows monthly expenses: Rent £450, Food £280, Transport £120, Other £150. What percentage of the total expenses is spent on Food?

questions.explanation: Multiply each score by its frequency and add: (0x2)+(1x3)+(2x4)+(3x1) = 0+3+8+3 = 14. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A frequency table shows goals scored by a football team in 10 matches: 0 goals (2 matches), 1 goal (3 matches), 2 goals (4 matches), 3 goals (1 match). What is the total number of goals scored across all matches?

questions.explanation: The mode is the value with the highest frequency. 1 sibling has the highest frequency (8 students), so the mode is 1. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A frequency table shows the number of siblings for 20 students: 0 siblings (5 students), 1 sibling (8 students), 2 siblings (5 students), 3 siblings (2 students). What is the modal number of siblings?

questions.explanation: Team Y's win rate: 18/24 = 75%. Since 75% is greater than 60%, Team Y has the better win rate. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Chart A shows Team X won 60% of their matches. Chart B shows Team Y won 18 out of 24 matches. Which team has the better win rate?

questions.explanation: Survey A: 3/4 of 80 = 60 people. Survey B: 65% of 100 = 65 people. Since 65 is more than 60, Survey B has more people preferring coffee, even though 3/4 (75%) is a higher proportion than 65%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Survey A shows 3/4 of 80 people prefer coffee. Survey B shows 65% of 100 people prefer coffee. In which survey do MORE people (in actual number) prefer coffee?

options.text: Survey A, because 3/4 is bigger than 65%

questions.explanation: Mean = (12+8+15+9)/4 = 44/4 = 11. Since 11 is greater than the target of 10, the school did not meet its goal. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A school records the number of absences per week over 4 weeks: 12, 8, 15, 9. If the school aims for an average of no more than 10 absences per week, did they meet this goal? Show your working.
questions.answer: No, the mean is 11, which is above the target of 10.

questions.stem: A shop's weekly sales over 5 weeks were: £2,400, £2,650, £1,980, £2,750, £2,220. What was the mean weekly sales?

questions.explanation: Shop A total: 20+35=55. Shop B total: 15+45=60. Since 60 is greater than 55, Shop B sold more overall, even though Shop A sold more in the morning. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A dual bar chart shows ice cream sales for two shops over a day: Morning - Shop A 20, Shop B 15; Afternoon - Shop A 35, Shop B 45. Which shop sold more ice creams in total across the whole day?

questions.explanation: City X total: 40+60=100. City Y total: 55+35=90. Since 100 is greater than 90, City X had more total rainfall. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A dual bar chart shows rainfall (mm) for two cities over 2 months: Month 1 - City X 40, City Y 55; Month 2 - City X 60, City Y 35. Which city had more total rainfall over the two months?

options.text: City Y, because 55 is more than 40

questions.explanation: 30 apples / 6 symbols = 5 apples per symbol. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A pictogram uses symbols to show fruit sales. 6 symbols represent 30 apples sold. What does each symbol represent?

questions.explanation: 27 items / 4.5 symbols = 6 items per symbol. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A pictogram shows that 4.5 symbols represent 27 items. What does each full symbol represent?

questions.explanation: The profit increases by £4,000 each year. Continuing the trend: 18,000+4,000=£22,000. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A line graph shows a company's profit increasing steadily: Year 1 £10,000, Year 2 £14,000, Year 3 £18,000. If this steady trend continues, what would you predict the profit to be in Year 4?

questions.explanation: The balance increases by £60 each month. Month 4: 320+60=£380. Month 5: 380+60=£440. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A line graph shows a savings account balance growing steadily: Month 1 £200, Month 2 £260, Month 3 £320. If the trend continues, what would the balance be in Month 5?

questions.explanation: All the percentages must add up to 100%: 100-35-25-20=20%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A pie chart shows favourite subjects: Maths 35%, English 25%, Science 20%, and Art makes up the rest. What percentage chose Art?

questions.explanation: All the sectors must add up to 360 degrees: 360-120-90-100=50 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A pie chart shows transport methods: Car 120 degrees, Bus 90 degrees, Walk 100 degrees, and Bike makes up the rest of the 360 degrees. How many degrees represent Bike?

questions.explanation: Add the boys and girls who like dogs: 12+9=21. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A two-way table shows favourite pets by gender: Boys who like dogs=12, boys who like cats=8; Girls who like dogs=9, girls who like cats=11. How many students in total like dogs?

questions.explanation: Add the passed and failed students in Class A: 18+4=22. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A two-way table shows exam results: Passed - Class A 18, Class B 22; Failed - Class A 4, Class B 3. How many students are in Class A in total?

questions.explanation: Add the frequencies for scores 0, 1 and 2: 1+2+4=7. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A frequency table shows test scores out of 5 for 20 students: score 0 (1 student), score 1 (2 students), score 2 (4 students), score 3 (6 students), score 4 (5 students), score 5 (2 students). How many students scored 2 or fewer?

questions.explanation: Add the frequencies for 2 pets and 3 pets: 9+5=14. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A frequency table shows the number of pets owned by 30 families: 0 pets (6 families), 1 pet (10 families), 2 pets (9 families), 3 pets (5 families). How many families own at least 2 pets?

questions.explanation: 3 gridlines above zero = 3 x 5 = 15. Halfway to the next gridline (5) adds 2.5. Total: 15+2.5=17.5. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bar chart's vertical axis is marked in intervals of 5, with gridlines at 0, 5, 10, 15, 20. A bar for 'Tuesday' reaches 3 gridlines above zero, plus a small amount that is halfway to the next gridline. What value does the bar represent?

questions.explanation: 2 gridlines above zero = 2 x 4 = 8. Three-quarters of the way to the next gridline (4) adds 3. Total: 8+3=11. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A bar chart's vertical axis is marked in intervals of 4, with gridlines at 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 20. A bar for 'Product A' reaches 2 gridlines above zero, plus three-quarters of the way to the next gridline. What value does the bar represent?

questions.explanation: A single class of 25 out of 900 students is a very small sample, and that one class might have different tastes to the rest of the school by chance, so the results may not reflect what the whole school actually prefers. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A student wants to find out the most popular lunch choice in their school of 900 students. They ask only the 25 students in their own class. Explain why this might not give a reliable result for the whole school.
questions.answer: The sample is too small and may not represent the whole school.

questions.explanation: A large, random sample drawn from across the whole school is far more likely to represent everyone's views fairly than a small or biased group, such as only friends, only one team, or only one year group. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Which of these would give the most reliable data about the favourite sport of an entire school of 800 students?

options.text: Randomly surveying 200 students from across all year groups
Asking only the school football team
Asking only students who play sport

questions.explanation: Add the values: 2+3+1+4+5=15. Divide by the number of matches: 15/5=3. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows the number of goals scored by a team in 5 matches: 2, 3, 1, 4, 5. What is the mean number of goals scored per match?

questions.explanation: Converting symbols to books: A=6, B=4, C=8, D=2. Total: 6+4+8+2=20. Mean: 20/4=5. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A pictogram shows books read by 4 students, where each symbol represents 2 books: Student A 3 symbols, Student B 2 symbols, Student C 4 symbols, Student D 1 symbol. What is the mean number of books read?

questions.explanation: Shop A's growth: (1,500/5,000) x 100 = 30%. Shop B's growth: (1,200/8,000) x 100 = 15%. Since 30% is greater than 15%, Shop A had the greater percentage growth, even though its actual pound increase was smaller. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Chart 1 shows Shop A's sales grew from £5,000 to £6,500 over a year. Chart 2 shows Shop B's sales grew from £8,000 to £9,200 over the same year. Which shop had the greater percentage growth?

questions.explanation: The question asks about performance on average, and Class A's average (68%) is higher than Class B's average (62%). The fact that more individual Class B students scored above 70% doesn't change the class-wide average comparison. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Table 1 shows Class A's average test score was 68%. Table 2 shows Class B's average test score was 62%, even though more individual students in Class B scored above 70% than in Class A. Which class performed better on average?

options.text: Class B, because more individual students passed

questions.explanation: Each leaf on the stem-4 row represents one student scoring in the 40s. There are 4 leaves (1, 4, 6, 9), so 4 students scored in the 40s. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf diagram shows test scores: stem 3 has leaves 2, 5, 8 (representing 32, 35, 38); stem 4 has leaves 1, 4, 6, 9 (representing 41, 44, 46, 49). How many students scored in the 40s?

questions.explanation: The highest stem is 3, with a leaf of 2, giving an age of 32 - the largest value shown in the diagram. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A stem-and-leaf diagram shows ages: stem 1 has leaves 8, 9 (18, 19); stem 2 has leaves 0, 3, 5, 7 (20, 23, 25, 27); stem 3 has leaf 2 (32). What is the oldest age recorded?

questions.explanation: The range is the highest value minus the lowest: 25-15=10. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows daily temperatures over a week: 18, 22, 15, 25, 19, 21, 17 (degrees C). What is the range of temperatures?

questions.explanation: The range is the highest value minus the lowest: £15-£5=£10. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A table shows weekly pocket money for 5 children: £8, £12, £5, £15, £10. What is the range?

questions.explanation: Order the ages: 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 18, 22. With 7 values, the median is the middle (4th) value: 14. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A table shows the ages of 7 people at a party: 12, 15, 9, 22, 18, 14, 11. What is the median age?

questions.explanation: With 8 values (already in order), the median is the mean of the 4th and 5th values: (6+6)/2=6. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A frequency table shows shoe sizes for 8 students: 4, 5, 5, 6, 6, 6, 7, 8. What is the median shoe size?

questions.explanation: Group A: 200 x 0.3 = 60 people. Group B: 160 x 0.4 = 64 people. Since 64 is greater than 60, Group B has more people who prefer tea, even from a smaller total. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Pie chart A (total 200 people) shows 30% prefer tea. Pie chart B (total 160 people) shows 40% prefer tea. Which group has more people (in actual number) who prefer tea?

questions.explanation: Group X: 300 x 0.25 = 75 people. Group Y: 220 x 0.35 = 77 people. Since 77 is greater than 75, Group Y has more people who cycle, despite having a smaller total. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Pie chart X (total 300 people) shows 25% cycle to work. Pie chart Y (total 220 people) shows 35% cycle to work. Which group has more people (in actual number) who cycle to work?

options.text: Group X, because 300 is a bigger total

questions.explanation: Total votes: 45+30+15+10=100. Candidate A's percentage: (45/100) x 100 = 45%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows votes for 4 candidates: A=45, B=30, C=15, D=10. What percentage of the total votes did Candidate A receive?

questions.explanation: Total sales: 200+150+100+50=500. Clothing's percentage: (150/500) x 100 = 30%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows sales by category: Electronics=200, Clothing=150, Food=100, Other=50. What percentage of sales came from Clothing?

questions.explanation: Increase = 65-40=25mph. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A line graph shows a car's speed over time: at 2pm it was 40mph, at 4pm it was 65mph. What was the increase in speed between these two times?

questions.explanation: Decrease = 120-85=35 litres. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A line graph shows a tank's water level: at 9am it was 120 litres, at 11am it was 85 litres. By how much did the water level decrease?

questions.explanation: 2 full groups of 5 = 10, plus 2 extra marks = 12 in total. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A tally chart shows votes using standard groups of 5: Red has 2 full groups of 5 plus 2 extra marks. How many people voted Red?

questions.explanation: 3 full groups of 5 = 15, plus 1 extra mark = 16 in total. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A tally chart shows pet ownership using standard groups of 5: Dogs has 3 full groups of 5 plus 1 extra mark. How many people own dogs?

questions.explanation: As one variable (revision time) increases, the other variable (test score) also tends to increase. This is called positive correlation. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A scatter graph shows that as students spend more time revising, their test scores tend to be higher. What type of correlation does this show?

questions.explanation: As one variable (temperature) increases, the other variable (hot chocolate sales) tends to decrease. This is called negative correlation. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A scatter graph shows that as the outdoor temperature increases, the number of hot chocolate drinks sold tends to decrease. What type of correlation does this show?

questions.explanation: 25% of 400 = 400 x 0.25 = 100 students. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows a school has 400 students in total. A pie chart shows that 25% of students walk to school. How many students walk to school?

questions.explanation: 60% of 250 = 250 x 0.6 = 150 customers. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows a shop had 250 customers in a week. A pie chart shows that 60% of customers made a purchase. How many customers made a purchase?

questions.explanation: Percentage = (52/80) x 100 = 65%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: In a survey of 80 people, 52 said they enjoy reading. What percentage of people surveyed enjoy reading?

questions.explanation: Percentage = (96/150) x 100 = 64%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: In a survey of 150 people, 96 said they prefer tea over coffee. What percentage prefer tea?

questions.explanation: Counting each value: 0 appears twice, 1 appears three times, 2 appears four times, 3 appears once. The mode (most frequent) is 2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows the number of pets owned by 10 families: 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 1, 0, 2. What is the modal number of pets?

questions.explanation: Size 7 was sold the most times (9), making it the mode. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows shoe sizes sold in a day: size 5 (4 sold), size 6 (7 sold), size 7 (9 sold), size 8 (5 sold). What is the modal shoe size sold?

questions.explanation: Apples: 3x8=24. Bananas: 2.5x8=20. Oranges: 4x8=32. Total: 24+20+32=76. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A pictogram shows fruit sold, where each symbol represents 8 items: Apples 3 symbols, Bananas 2.5 symbols, Oranges 4 symbols. What is the total number of fruit sold?

questions.explanation: Fiction: 5x6=30. Non-fiction: 3.5x6=21. Comics: 2x6=12. Total: 30+21+12=63. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A pictogram shows books borrowed, where each symbol represents 6 books: Fiction 5 symbols, Non-fiction 3.5 symbols, Comics 2 symbols. What is the total number of books borrowed?

questions.explanation: City B's temperature went from 15C to 20C, an increase of 20-15=5 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Two line graphs show the temperatures in two cities over a day. At 12pm, City A was 18C and City B was 15C. At 6pm, City A was 14C and City B was 20C. By how many degrees did City B's temperature change from 12pm to 6pm?

questions.explanation: Shop X's increase: 500-200=£300. Shop Y's increase: 380-350=£30. Shop X had the much greater increase, even though Shop Y started with more sales. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Two line graphs show sales for two shops. At 10am, Shop X had £200 and Shop Y had £350. By 2pm, Shop X had £500 and Shop Y had £380. Which shop had the greater increase in sales between these times?

options.text: Shop Y, because it started higher

questions.explanation: 150:120 can be simplified by dividing both by their highest common factor, 30: 150/30=5, 120/30=4, giving 5:4. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A pie chart shows favourite pets: Dogs 150 degrees, Cats 120 degrees, Other 90 degrees. Express the ratio of Dogs to Cats in its simplest form.

questions.explanation: 180:90:90 can be simplified by dividing all parts by 90: 180/90=2, 90/90=1, 90/90=1, giving 2:1:1. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A pie chart shows travel methods: Car 180 degrees, Bus 90 degrees, Walk 90 degrees. Express the ratio of Car to Bus to Walk in its simplest form.

questions.explanation: Class A's mean: (60+72+68+75+70)/5=345/5=69. Class B's mean: (65+70+72+68+80)/5=355/5=71. Since 71 is greater than 69, Class B has the higher mean. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Table 1 shows Class A's test scores: 60, 72, 68, 75, 70. Table 2 shows Class B's scores: 65, 70, 72, 68, 80. Which class has the higher mean score?

questions.explanation: Team X's mean: (12+18+15+9)/4=54/4=13.5. Team Y's mean: (14+16+13+17)/4=60/4=15. Since 15 is greater than 13.5, Team Y has the higher mean. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Table 1 shows Team X's points in 4 games: 12, 18, 15, 9. Table 2 shows Team Y's points: 14, 16, 13, 17. Which team has the higher mean points per game?

options.text: Team X, because 18 is the highest single score

questions.explanation: Multiply each midpoint by its frequency and add: (4.5x5)+(14.5x8)+(24.5x7)=22.5+116+171.5=310. Divide by the total number of people: 310/20=15.5. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A grouped frequency table shows ages: 0-9 (5 people, midpoint 4.5), 10-19 (8 people, midpoint 14.5), 20-29 (7 people, midpoint 24.5). Estimate the mean age using midpoints.

questions.explanation: Multiply each midpoint by its frequency and add: (144.5x4)+(154.5x10)+(164.5x6)=578+1545+987=3110. Divide by the total number of people: 3110/20=155.5cm. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A grouped frequency table shows heights: 140-149cm (midpoint 144.5, 4 people), 150-159cm (midpoint 154.5, 10 people), 160-169cm (midpoint 164.5, 6 people). Estimate the mean height using midpoints.

questions.explanation: Add the known days: 120+95+140=355. Subtract from the total: 500-355=145. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows the number of visitors to a museum over 4 days, totalling 500. Monday=120, Tuesday=95, Wednesday=140, and Thursday is missing. How many visitors came on Thursday?

questions.explanation: Add the known quarters: 520+680+610=1,810. Subtract from the total: 2,400-1,810=£590. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows sales over 4 quarters totalling £2,400. Q1=£520, Q2=£680, Q3=£610, and Q4 is missing. What is the value for Q4?

questions.explanation: The known percentages add up to 35+20+15+10=80%, so Other is 100-80=20%. Amount: 3,000 x 0.2 = £600. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A pie chart shows a family's monthly income of £3,000 split as: Housing 35%, Food 20%, Transport 15%, Savings 10%, and the rest on Other. How much is spent on 'Other'?

questions.explanation: The known percentages add up to 55+20+15=90%, so Utilities is 100-90=10%. Amount: 50,000 x 0.1 = £5,000. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A pie chart shows a company's £50,000 monthly costs split as: Wages 55%, Rent 20%, Materials 15%, and the rest on Utilities. How much is spent on Utilities?

questions.explanation: The mean is (22+24+25+26+95)/5=192/5=£38.4k, which is much higher than what most employees actually earn because of the outlier. The median, £25k, sits in the middle of the data and better reflects a typical salary. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A small company's salaries are: £22k, £24k, £25k, £26k, £95k (the owner). Which average, the mean or the median, better represents a 'typical' salary at this company, and why?
questions.answer: The median (£25k), because the mean is skewed upward by the owner's very high salary

questions.explanation: The mean uses every value in its calculation, so a single very large value like £1,200 pulls it upward significantly. The median, being the middle value when ordered, is much less affected by one extreme value. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A small shop's daily sales over 5 days were: £180, £190, £200, £210, £1,200 (an unusually busy day). Which average would be more affected by the unusual day: the mean or the median?

questions.explanation: Increase: 52,000-40,000=£12,000. Percentage increase: (12,000/40,000) x 100 = 30%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows a company's profit: last year £40,000, this year £52,000. What is the percentage increase in profit?

questions.explanation: Decrease: 250-220=30. Percentage decrease: (30/250) x 100 = 12%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A bar chart shows a shop's customer numbers: last month 250, this month 220. What is the percentage decrease in customers?

questions.explanation: Cost of books: 3 x 8.50 = £25.50. Adding the magazine: 25.50 + 3.25 = £28.75. Money left: 45 - 28.75 = £16.25. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Ella has £45. She buys 3 books at £8.50 each and a magazine for £3.25. How much money does she have left?

questions.explanation: Spent on the game: 60 x 2/5 = £24, leaving 60-24=£36. After lunch: 36-12=£24. A common mistake is applying the fraction to the wrong amount or forgetting one of the two spending steps. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Tom starts with £60. He spends 2/5 of it on a game, then £12 on lunch. How much does he have left?

questions.explanation: Convert the rope to centimetres: 4.5m=450cm. Total cut: 3x80=240cm. Remaining: 450-240=210cm=2.1m. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A rope is 4.5m long. Three pieces of 80cm each are cut off. How much rope is left, in metres?

questions.explanation: Total poured out: 4.2+3.8+2.5=10.5L. Remaining: 15-10.5=4.5L. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A tank holds 15 litres. Water is poured out in 3 stages: 4.2L, 3.8L and 2.5L. How much water remains, in litres?

questions.explanation: Journey A: 1 hour 45 minutes = 105 minutes. Journey B: 115 minutes. Since 105 is less than 115, Journey A is shorter, by 115-105=10 minutes. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Journey A takes 1 hour 45 minutes. Journey B takes 115 minutes. Which journey is shorter, and by how many minutes?

questions.explanation: Recipe A: 750/6=125g per person. Recipe B: 900/8=112.5g per person. Since 112.5 is less than 125, Recipe B uses less flour per person, even though it uses more flour overall. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Recipe A needs 750g of flour for 6 people. Recipe B needs 900g of flour for 8 people. Which recipe uses less flour per person?

options.text: Recipe A, because 750 is less than 900

questions.explanation: Work backwards: before spending on food, Sam had 22 x 2 = £44 (since £22 was half of what remained). Before the entry fee, Sam had 44+15=£59. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: After paying a £15 entry fee and then spending half of what remained on food, Sam had £22 left. How much money did Sam start with?

questions.explanation: Work backwards: before losing 5, Leo had 19+5=24 marbles, which represents 2/3 of his original amount (since 1/3 was given away). So 1/3 = 24/2=12, and the original total = 12x3=36. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: After giving away 1/3 of his marbles, then losing 5 more, Leo had 19 marbles left. How many marbles did he start with?

questions.explanation: Pipe A fills 1/6 of the tank per hour, Pipe B fills 1/3 per hour. Combined rate: 1/6+1/3=1/6+2/6=3/6=1/2 of the tank per hour. Time to fill: 1/(1/2)=2 hours. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Pipe A can fill a tank in 6 hours. Pipe B can fill the same tank in 3 hours. If both pipes work together, how long will it take to fill the tank?

questions.explanation: Machine A completes 1/4 of the job per hour, Machine B completes 1/12 per hour. Combined rate: 3/12+1/12=4/12=1/3 of the job per hour. Time to complete: 1/(1/3)=3 hours. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Machine A can complete a job in 4 hours. Machine B can complete the same job in 12 hours. Working together, how long will it take?

questions.explanation: Let the first child get x sweets. The others get x+2 and x+4. Total: x+(x+2)+(x+4)=3x+6=42, so 3x=36 and x=12. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: 42 sweets are shared among 3 children so that each child after the first gets 2 more sweets than the previous one. How many sweets does the first child get?

questions.explanation: Let the first friend get x stickers. The others get x+3, x+6, x+9. Total: 4x+18=66, so 4x=48 and x=12. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: 66 stickers are shared among 4 friends so that each friend after the first gets 3 more stickers than the previous one. How many stickers does the first friend get?

questions.explanation: Cost of first type: 8x3=£24. Cost of second type: 12x5=£60. Total: 24+60=£84. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A shopkeeper mixes 8kg of nuts costing £3/kg with 12kg of nuts costing £5/kg. What is the total cost of the mixture?

questions.explanation: Cost of first type: 5x2.40=£12. Cost of second type: 3x4.00=£12. Total: 12+12=£24. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A gardener mixes 5L of fertiliser costing £2.40/L with 3L costing £4.00/L. What is the total cost?

questions.explanation: Sold: 240 x 0.25=60, leaving 240-60=180. Moved to new field: 180 x 1/4=45. Remaining in original field: 180-45=135. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A farmer has 240 sheep. 25% are sold, and then 1/4 of the remaining sheep are moved to a new field. How many sheep remain in the original field?

questions.explanation: Leave: 300 x 0.15=45, leaving 300-45=255. Retire: 255 x 1/5=51. Remaining: 255-51=204. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A company has 300 employees. 15% leave the company, and then 1/5 of the remaining employees retire. How many employees are left?

questions.explanation: Students playing at least one sport: 18+12-5=25 (subtracting the overlap once, since they were counted in both groups). Students playing neither: 30-25=5. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: In a class of 30 students, 18 play football, 12 play tennis, and 5 play both sports. How many students play neither sport?

questions.explanation: People who like at least one drink: 28+22-10=40. People who like neither: 50-40=10. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: In a survey of 50 people, 28 like tea, 22 like coffee, and 10 like both. How many people like neither?

questions.explanation: Dana likes red and Beth likes green, so those colours are taken. Alex doesn't like red or blue, and green is already taken by Beth, so Alex must like yellow. This leaves blue for Chris, which fits since Chris doesn't like yellow. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Four children - Alex, Beth, Chris and Dana - each have a different favourite colour: red, blue, green, yellow. Alex doesn't like red or blue. Beth likes green. Chris doesn't like yellow. Dana likes red. What colour does Alex like?

questions.explanation: Tia doesn't own the cat or the dog, so Tia must own the rabbit. Sam doesn't own the dog, so Sam must own the cat, leaving the dog for Uma. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Three friends - Sam, Tia and Uma - each own a different pet: cat, dog, rabbit. Sam doesn't own the dog. Tia doesn't own the cat or the dog. What pet does Uma own?

questions.explanation: First meeting ends: 10:15 + 1:40 = 11:55am. After the 20-minute break: 11:55 + 0:20 = 12:15pm. Second meeting ends: 12:15 + 0:45 = 1:00pm. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A meeting starts at 10:15am and lasts 1 hour 40 minutes. After a 20-minute break, a second meeting begins and lasts 45 minutes. What time does the second meeting end?

questions.explanation: First film ends: 7:20 + 2:15 = 9:35pm. After the interval: 9:35 + 0:15 = 9:50pm. Second film (95 minutes = 1h35m) ends: 9:50 + 1:35 = 11:25pm. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A film starts at 7:20pm and lasts 2 hours 15 minutes. After a 15-minute interval, a second film starts and lasts 95 minutes. What time does the second film end?

questions.explanation: The ratio parts add up to 8, so each part is worth 480/8=£60. The larger share (5 parts): 5x60=£300. Donation: 10% of 300=£30. Amount left: 300-30=£270. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A prize fund of £480 is shared between two teams in the ratio 5:3. The team with the larger share then donates 10% of their winnings to charity. How much does that team have left?

questions.explanation: The ratio parts add up to 5, so each part is worth 600/5=£120. The larger share (3 parts): 3x120=£360. Admin costs: 1/4 of 360=£90. Amount left: 360-90=£270. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A £600 fund is split between two charities in the ratio 2:3. The charity with the larger share spends 1/4 of their amount on admin costs. How much do they have left for their cause?

questions.explanation: Total distance: 400 x 6 = 2,400m, which is 2.4km. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A running track is 400m around. If Priya runs 6 laps, how far has she run in kilometres?

questions.explanation: Perimeter: 2 x (120+80) = 400m. Total distance for 3 laps: 400 x 3 = 1,200m = 1.2km. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A rectangular field measures 120m by 80m. Ben jogs around the perimeter 3 times. How far has he jogged in total, in kilometres?

questions.explanation: Friend A is busy on days that are multiples of 3, and Friend B on multiples of 4. The next day both are busy together is the lowest common multiple of 3 and 4, which is 12. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Two friends are free to meet up: Friend A is busy every 3rd day starting today. Friend B is busy every 4th day starting today. On which day (counting today as day 0) are both friends next busy at the same time?

questions.explanation: Both joggers return to the start together after a time that is a multiple of both 5 and 8, which is their lowest common multiple: 40 minutes. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Two joggers start running around a track at the same time. Jogger X completes a lap every 5 minutes. Jogger Y completes a lap every 8 minutes. After how many minutes will they both be back at the starting point together?

questions.explanation: Total needed for 4 tests: 72x4=288. The first three scores add up to 68+75+70=213. The fourth score: 288-213=75. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A student's average score across 4 tests is 72. If the first three test scores were 68, 75 and 70, what was the fourth score?

questions.explanation: Total needed for 3 stages: 24x3=72. The first two speeds add up to 20+22=42. The third stage's speed: 72-42=30km/h. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A cyclist's average speed over 3 stages was 24km/h. If the first two stages had average speeds of 20km/h and 22km/h, what was the average speed of the third stage?

questions.explanation: 137 / 6 = 22 remainder 5. This means 22 full boxes plus one more box for the remaining 5 muffins, so 23 boxes are needed in total, with the last box containing 5 muffins. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A baker has 137 muffins to pack into boxes of 6. How many boxes are needed to pack all the muffins, and how many muffins will be in the last (not-full) box?
questions.answer: 23 boxes, with 5 muffins in the last box

questions.explanation: 95 / 8 = 11 remainder 7. This means 11 full bunches can be made, with 7 flowers left over. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A florist has 95 flowers to arrange into bunches of 8. How many full bunches can be made, and how many flowers are left over?

questions.explanation: Even numbers between 20 and 30 (exclusive): 22, 24, 26, 28. Of these, only 24 is divisible by 3. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: I am thinking of a number. It is even, greater than 20 but less than 30, and divisible by 3. What is the number?

questions.explanation: Multiples of 4 between 30 and 45: 32, 36, 40, 44. Of these, only 36 is also a multiple of 6. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: I am thinking of a number. It is a multiple of 4, greater than 30 but less than 45, and also a multiple of 6. What is the number?

questions.explanation: After the 20% discount: 80x0.8=£64. Taking off the further £5: 64-5=£59. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A jacket costs £80. A store discount of 20% is applied, then a loyalty card gives a further £5 off the discounted price. What is the final price?

questions.explanation: After the 15% discount: 600x0.85=£510. Taking off the further £30: 510-30=£480. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A laptop costs £600. A sale discount of 15% is applied, then a student discount of £30 is taken off the sale price. What is the final price?

questions.explanation: These are triangular numbers: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 (each total adds one more than the previous gap). By step 5, the cumulative total is 15 blocks. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A staircase pattern uses cumulative block totals: 1 block for step 1, 3 blocks in total by step 2, 6 blocks in total by step 3, 10 blocks in total by step 4. Following this pattern, how many blocks in total would be needed to build 5 steps?

questions.explanation: Each design's tile count follows the rule n(n+1): design 1 = 1x2=2, design 2=2x3=6, design 3=3x4=12, design 4=4x5=20. Design 6 = 6x7=42. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A pattern of coloured tiles uses: 2 tiles for design 1, 6 tiles for design 2, 12 tiles for design 3, 20 tiles for design 4. How many tiles would design 6 need?

questions.explanation: Let the number be x. The equation is 2x-8=x+6. Subtracting x from both sides: x-8=6, so x=14. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: If a number is doubled and then 8 is subtracted, the result is the same as the original number plus 6. What is the number?

questions.explanation: Let the number be x. The equation is 3x-10=x+20. Subtracting x from both sides: 2x-10=20, so 2x=30 and x=15. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: If a number is tripled and then 10 is subtracted, the result is the same as the original number plus 20. What is the number?

questions.explanation: Transport and food together: 150+120=£270. Activities: 360-270=£90. As a fraction of the total: 90/360=1/4. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A youth club has £360 to spend on a trip. £150 goes on transport, £120 on food, and the rest on activities. What fraction of the total budget is spent on activities?

questions.explanation: Venue, catering and photography together: 3,200+2,000+1,200=£6,400. Flowers: 8,000-6,400=£1,600. As a percentage: (1,600/8,000)x100=20%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A wedding budget of £8,000 is split: £3,200 on venue, £2,000 on catering, £1,200 on photography, and the rest on flowers. What percentage of the budget is spent on flowers?

questions.explanation: Let the numbers be n, n+2, n+4. Their sum is 3n+6=90, so 3n=84 and n=28. The numbers are 28, 30 and 32. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: The sum of three consecutive EVEN numbers is 90. What are the three numbers?

questions.explanation: Let the numbers be n, n+2, n+4, n+6. Their sum is 4n+12=96, so 4n=84 and n=21. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: The sum of four consecutive ODD numbers is 96. What is the smallest of the four numbers?

questions.explanation: Total dollars after exchange: 200 x 1.30 = $260. After spending: 260-150=$110. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Tom exchanges £200 at a rate of £1 = $1.30. He then spends $150 on souvenirs. How many dollars does he have left?

questions.explanation: Total euros after exchange: 350 x 1.15 = €402.50. After spending: 402.50-250=€152.50. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Priya exchanges £350 at a rate of £1 = €1.15. She then spends €250 on a hotel. How many euros does she have left?

questions.explanation: Plan A: 25/5=£5 per GB. Plan B: 30/8=£3.75 per GB. Plan C: 20/3=£6.67 per GB (approx). Plan B has the lowest cost per GB, making it the best value, even though it isn't the cheapest overall. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Three phone plans cost: Plan A £25/month with 5GB data, Plan B £30/month with 8GB data, Plan C £20/month with 3GB data. Which plan offers the best value in terms of cost per GB?

questions.explanation: Cafe X: 7.50/3=£2.50 per cup. Cafe Y: 9.20/4=£2.30 per cup. Cafe Z: 11.00/5=£2.20 per cup. Cafe Z has the lowest price per cup. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Three cafes sell coffee: Cafe X 3 cups for £7.50, Cafe Y 4 cups for £9.20, Cafe Z 5 cups for £11.00. Which cafe offers the cheapest price per cup?

options.text: Cafe X, because it has the fewest cups

questions.explanation: Total liquid: 2+3.5=5.5 litres. Container B's capacity is only 5 litres, so it becomes completely full, and the remaining 5.5-5=0.5 litres cannot fit and would overflow. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Container A holds 3.5 litres and is full. Container B holds 5 litres and has 2 litres in it. If all the liquid from Container A is poured into Container B, how much liquid ends up in Container B, and is there any left over?
questions.answer: Container B becomes full at 5 litres, with 0.5 litres unable to fit (overflow)

questions.explanation: Total liquid: 3+6=9 litres, which fits within Container X's 10-litre capacity with no overflow. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Container X holds 10 litres and has 3 litres in it. Container Y holds 6 litres and is full. If all the liquid from Container Y is poured into Container X, how much liquid is in Container X now?

questions.explanation: Area of a circle = pi x r^2 = 3.14 x 7^2 = 3.14 x 49 = 153.86cm^2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Find the area of a circle with radius 7cm. Use pi = 3.14.

questions.explanation: Area of a circle = pi x r^2 = 3.14 x 5^2 = 3.14 x 25 = 78.5cm^2. A common mistake is using the diameter instead of the radius, or forgetting to square the radius. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Find the area of a circle with radius 5cm. Use pi = 3.14.

questions.explanation: Circumference = pi x diameter = 3.14 x 10 = 31.4cm. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Find the circumference of a circle with diameter 10cm. Use pi = 3.14.

questions.explanation: Circumference = 2 x pi x radius = 2 x 3.14 x 6 = 37.68cm. A common mistake is using the radius directly in the diameter formula without doubling it first. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Find the circumference of a circle with radius 6cm. Use pi = 3.14.

questions.explanation: Cross-sectional area = 0.5 x 6 x 4 = 12cm^2. Volume = cross-sectional area x length = 12 x 10 = 120cm^3. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A triangular prism has a triangular cross-section with base 6cm and height 4cm, and a length of 10cm. Find its volume.

questions.explanation: Cross-sectional area = 0.5 x 8 x 5 = 20cm^2. Volume = 20 x 12 = 240cm^3. A common mistake is forgetting to halve the base x height when finding the triangle's area. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A triangular prism has a triangular cross-section with base 8cm and height 5cm, and a length of 12cm. Find its volume.

questions.explanation: Surface area = 2 x (lw+lh+wh) = 2 x (15+20+12) = 2 x 47 = 94cm^2. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Find the surface area of a cuboid with length 5cm, width 3cm and height 4cm.

questions.explanation: Surface area = 2 x (lw+lh+wh) = 2 x (24+12+8) = 2 x 44 = 88cm^2. A common mistake is only calculating 3 faces instead of all 6 (missing the doubling step). (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Find the surface area of a cuboid with length 6cm, width 4cm and height 2cm.

questions.explanation: A cube has 6 identical square faces. Surface area = 6 x (side x side) = 6 x 36 = 216cm^2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Find the surface area of a cube with side length 6cm.

questions.explanation: Surface area = 6 x (4x4) = 6 x 16 = 96cm^2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Find the surface area of a cube with side length 4cm.

questions.explanation: Volume of first cuboid: 4x3x2=24cm^3. Volume of second cuboid: 5x3x2=30cm^3. Total: 24+30=54cm^3. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A 3D shape is made of two cuboids joined together: one measuring 4cm x 3cm x 2cm and another measuring 5cm x 3cm x 2cm. Find the total volume.

questions.explanation: Volume of the full cuboid: 6x4x3=72cm^3. Volume removed: 2x4x3=24cm^3. Remaining: 72-24=48cm^3. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A composite shape is made from a cuboid 6cm x 4cm x 3cm with a smaller cuboid 2cm x 4cm x 3cm removed from one end. Find the remaining volume.

questions.explanation: Full circle area = 3.14 x 8^2 = 3.14 x 64 = 200.96cm^2. Halving for the semicircle: 200.96/2=100.48cm^2. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Find the area of a semicircle with radius 8cm. Use pi = 3.14.

questions.explanation: Full circle area = 3.14 x 4^2 = 3.14 x 16 = 50.24cm^2. Halving for the semicircle: 50.24/2=25.12cm^2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Find the area of a semicircle with radius 4cm. Use pi = 3.14.

questions.explanation: New area = 8x8=64cm^2. The area has increased by a factor of 64/16=4, not 2. This is because doubling BOTH dimensions (length and width) of a square multiplies the area by 2x2=4. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A square has a side length of 4cm and an area of 16cm^2. If the side length is doubled to 8cm, what is the new area, and by what factor has the area increased?
questions.answer: 64cm^2, an increase by a factor of 4

questions.explanation: Tripling the side length multiplies both the length and width dimensions by 3, so the area increases by a factor of 3x3=9. A common mistake is assuming the area also just triples. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A square has a side length of 5cm. If the side length is tripled, by what factor does the area increase?

questions.explanation: Volume = 12x6x1.5=108m^3. Converting to litres: 108 x 1,000 = 108,000 litres. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A swimming pool is a cuboid measuring 12m long, 6m wide and 1.5m deep. How many litres of water are needed to fill it completely? (1m^3 = 1,000 litres)

questions.explanation: Volume = 2x1.5x1=3m^3. Converting to litres: 3 x 1,000 = 3,000 litres. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A water tank is a cuboid measuring 2m by 1.5m by 1m. How many litres does it hold when full? (1m^3 = 1,000 litres)

questions.explanation: Circumference = pi x diameter = 3.14 x 70 = 219.8cm, which rounds to 220cm. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bicycle wheel has a diameter of 70cm. Using pi = 3.14, find how far the bike travels in one full rotation of the wheel, to the nearest cm.

questions.explanation: Circumference = 2 x pi x radius = 2 x 3.14 x 50 = 314m. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A circular running track has a radius of 50m. Using pi = 3.14, find the distance covered in one lap, to the nearest metre.

questions.explanation: Two triangular faces: 2 x (0.5x6x4) = 24cm^2. Three rectangular faces: 10 x (6+5+5) = 10x16 = 160cm^2. Total: 24+160=184cm^2. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A triangular prism has two triangular faces with base 6cm and height 4cm, and three rectangular faces along its length of 10cm with widths of 6cm, 5cm and 5cm (the three sides of the triangle). Find the total surface area.

questions.explanation: Two triangular faces: 2 x (0.5x8x3) = 24cm^2. Three rectangular faces: 12 x (8+5+5) = 12x18 = 216cm^2. Total: 24+216=240cm^2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A triangular prism has two triangular faces with base 8cm and height 3cm, and three rectangular faces along its length of 12cm with widths of 8cm, 5cm and 5cm. Find the total surface area.

questions.explanation: Area of 2 circular ends: 2 x 3.14 x 5^2 = 2 x 78.5 = 157cm^2. Curved surface area: 2 x 3.14 x 5 x 10 = 314cm^2. Total: 157+314=471cm^2. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A cylinder has radius 5cm and height 10cm. Using pi=3.14, find its total surface area (2 circular ends plus the curved surface).

questions.explanation: Area of 2 circular ends: 2 x 3.14 x 3^2 = 56.52cm^2. Curved surface area: 2 x 3.14 x 3 x 8 = 150.72cm^2. Total: 56.52+150.72=207.24cm^2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A cylinder has radius 3cm and height 8cm. Using pi=3.14, find its total surface area.

questions.explanation: Volume = pi x r^2 x h = 3.14 x 16 x 10 = 502.4cm^3. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A cylinder has radius 4cm and height 10cm. Using pi=3.14, find its volume.

questions.explanation: Volume = pi x r^2 x h = 3.14 x 36 x 5 = 565.2cm^3. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A cylinder has radius 6cm and height 5cm. Using pi=3.14, find its volume.

questions.explanation: New volume = 6x6x6=216cm^3. The volume has increased by a factor of 216/27=8, not 2. Doubling all 3 dimensions multiplies the volume by 2x2x2=8. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A cube has a side length of 3cm and a volume of 27cm^3. If the side length is doubled to 6cm, what is the new volume, and by what factor has the volume increased?
questions.answer: 216cm^3, an increase by a factor of 8

questions.explanation: Tripling all 3 dimensions multiplies the volume by 3x3x3=27. A common mistake is assuming the volume also just triples. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A cube has a side length of 2cm. If the side length is tripled, by what factor does the volume increase?

questions.explanation: Perimeter includes: 2 long sides (10cm each) = 20cm, 1 remaining short side = 6cm, and the curved semicircle edge = half the circumference = (3.14x6)/2=9.42cm. Total: 20+6+9.42=35.42cm. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A shape is made from a rectangle 10cm by 6cm, with a semicircle of diameter 6cm attached to one of the shorter sides (replacing that side). Using pi=3.14, find the total perimeter of the shape.

questions.explanation: Perimeter includes: 2 long sides (8cm each) = 16cm, 1 remaining short side = 5cm, and the curved semicircle edge = (3.14x5)/2=7.85cm. Total: 16+5+7.85=28.85cm. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A shape is made from a rectangle 8cm by 5cm, with a semicircle of diameter 5cm attached to one of the shorter sides (replacing that side). Using pi=3.14, find the total perimeter.

questions.explanation: Rectangle area: 10x6=60cm^2. Semicircle (radius 3): 0.5x3.14x3^2=14.13cm^2. Total: 60+14.13=74.13cm^2. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A shape is made from a rectangle 10cm by 6cm, with a semicircle of diameter 6cm attached to one of the shorter sides. Using pi=3.14, find the total area.

questions.explanation: Rectangle area: 8x5=40cm^2. Semicircle (radius 2.5): 0.5x3.14x2.5^2=9.81cm^2. Total: 40+9.81=49.81cm^2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A shape is made from a rectangle 8cm by 5cm, with a semicircle of diameter 5cm attached to one of the shorter sides. Using pi=3.14, find the total area.
