questions.explanation: Rearranging area = pi x r^2: r^2 = 78.5/3.14=25, so r = square root of 25 = 5cm. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A circle has an area of 78.5cm^2. Using pi=3.14, find its radius.

questions.explanation: Rearranging area = pi x r^2: r^2 = 200.96/3.14=64, so r = square root of 64 = 8cm. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A circle has an area of 200.96cm^2. Using pi=3.14, find its radius.

questions.explanation: Rearranging circumference = 2 x pi x r: r = 44/(2x3.14)=44/6.28=7.0cm (to 1 decimal place). (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A circle has a circumference of 44cm. Using pi=3.14, find its radius, to 1 decimal place.

questions.explanation: Rearranging circumference = 2 x pi x r: r = 62.8/(2x3.14)=62.8/6.28=10cm. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A circle has a circumference of 62.8cm. Using pi=3.14, find its radius.

questions.explanation: Container A's volume: 4x5x6=120cm^3. Container B's volume: 5x5x5=125cm^3. Since 125 is greater than 120, Container B has the greater volume. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Container A is a cuboid measuring 4cm x 5cm x 6cm. Container B is a cube with side length 5cm. Which container has the greater volume?

questions.explanation: Container X's volume: 3.14x3^2x10=282.6cm^3. Container Y's volume: 6x5x4=120cm^3. Since 282.6 is greater than 120, Container X has the greater volume. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Container X is a cylinder with radius 3cm and height 10cm (use pi=3.14). Container Y is a cuboid measuring 6cm x 5cm x 4cm. Which container has the greater volume?

options.text: Container Y, because it has more straight edges

questions.explanation: Density = mass / volume = 540/60=9g/cm^3. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)

questions.stem: Find the area of a quarter circle with radius 10cm. Use pi=3.14.

questions.stem: Find the area of a quarter circle with radius 6cm. Use pi=3.14.

questions.stem: A cuboid has a volume of 240cm^3, a length of 8cm and a width of 6cm. Find its height.

questions.stem: A cylinder has a volume of 942cm^3 and a height of 12cm. Using pi=3.14, find its radius.

questions.stem: A ring shape has an outer radius of 10cm and an inner radius of 6cm. Using pi=3.14, find the area of the ring.

questions.explanation: Outer circle area: 3.14 x 8^2 = 200.96cm^2. Inner circle area: 3.14 x 5^2 = 78.5cm^2. Area of the ring: 200.96-78.5=122.46cm^2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A ring shape has an outer radius of 8cm and an inner radius of 5cm. Using pi=3.14, find the area of the ring.

questions.explanation: Volume = pi x r^2 x h = 3.14 x 16 x 20 = 1,004.8cm^3, which is 1,004.8ml. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A cylindrical water bottle has a radius of 4cm and a height of 20cm. Using pi=3.14, find its capacity in millilitres (1cm^3=1ml).

questions.stem: A cylindrical can has a radius of 3cm and a height of 12cm. Using pi=3.14, find its capacity in millilitres.

questions.stem: A wall measures 5m by 3m. One tin of paint covers 7.5m^2. How many tins are needed to paint the wall (assuming you can't buy part of a tin)?

questions.stem: 145 children need to be transported by minibus, each holding 18 children. How many minibuses are needed?

questions.stem: Work out 45 divided by 8, giving your answer as a decimal.

questions.explanation: 15+27=42 and 27+15=42. Addition is commutative, meaning the order of the numbers does not affect the total. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Does the order matter when adding 15+27 compared to 27+15? Give both totals and explain briefly.

questions.explanation: For subtraction, a-b does not generally equal b-a (for example, 10-4=6 but 4-10=-6). Addition and multiplication are both commutative, since changing the order does not affect the result. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Which of these operations is NOT commutative (meaning the order does matter)?

questions.explanation: 34x10=340. Adding 34 more (x1): 340+34=374. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Use a mental strategy to work out 34 x 11 quickly (hint: x11 = x10 + x1).

questions.stem: Use a mental strategy to work out 47 x 9 quickly (hint: x9 = x10 - x1).

questions.stem: Is 4,572 divisible by 3? Use the digit-sum rule to check, and explain your answer.

questions.stem: Is 2,835 divisible by 9? Use the digit-sum rule to check.

questions.stem: Find the value of y that makes both sides equal: 3 x y = 18 + 24.

questions.explanation: Sold in the morning: 240x3/4=180, leaving 240-180=60. After baking 60 more: 60+60=120. Selling half: 120/2=60 sold, leaving 120-60=60 loaves. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A bakery bakes 240 loaves of bread. They sell 3/4 of them in the morning, then bake 60 more loaves in the afternoon, and sell half of the total remaining stock by the end of the day. How many loaves are left at the end of the day?

questions.explanation: Sold at market: 500x2/5=200, leaving 500-200=300. After picking 150 more: 300+150=450. Giving away a third: 450/3=150, leaving 450-150=300. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A farmer has 500 apples. He sells 2/5 of them at a market, then picks 150 more apples, and gives away a third of the new total to a food bank. How many apples does he have left?

questions.explanation: Adding 7 five times is the same as 7 multiplied by 5: 7x5=35. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Write 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 + 7 as a multiplication, and give the total.

questions.explanation: Adding 12 four times is the same as 12 multiplied by 4: 12x4=48. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Write 12 + 12 + 12 + 12 as a multiplication, and give the total.

questions.explanation: To check a subtraction, add the answer back to the number subtracted: 47+37=84, which matches the original number, so the calculation is correct. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A student calculates 84 minus 37 = 47. Use the inverse operation (addition) to check if this is correct.

questions.explanation: To check a division, multiply the answer by the divisor: 13x12=156, which matches the original number, so the calculation is correct. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A student calculates 156 divided by 12 = 13. Use the inverse operation (multiplication) to check if this is correct.

questions.explanation: The smallest share is 2 parts, worth £18, so 1 part is worth 18/2=£9. The total is 10 parts (2+3+5): 9x10=£90. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Money is shared in the ratio 2:3:5. If the smallest share is £18, what is the total amount shared?

questions.explanation: The middle share is 4 parts, worth 16 sweets, so 1 part is worth 16/4=4. The total is 12 parts (3+4+5): 4x12=48. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Sweets are shared in the ratio 3:4:5. If the middle share is 16 sweets, what is the total number of sweets?

questions.explanation: To combine, make the 'b' term match in both ratios. a:b=2:3 becomes 8:12 (multiplying by 4). b:c=4:5 becomes 12:15 (multiplying by 3). Now both have b=12, giving a:b:c=8:12:15. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: If a:b=2:3 and b:c=4:5, find the ratio a:b:c.

questions.explanation: To combine, make the 'y' term match. x:y=3:4 already has y=4. y:z=2:5 becomes 4:10 (multiplying by 2). Now both have y=4, giving x:y:z=3:4:10. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: If x:y=3:4 and y:z=2:5, find the ratio x:y:z.

questions.explanation: Rate per metre: 6/4=£1.50 per metre. Cost for 10m: 1.50x10=£15. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: The cost of rope is directly proportional to its length. 4m of rope costs £6. How much would 10m of rope cost?

questions.explanation: Rate: 12/300=0.04 biscuits per gram. For 500g: 0.04x500=20 biscuits. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: The number of biscuits made is directly proportional to the amount of flour used. 300g of flour makes 12 biscuits. How many biscuits can be made with 500g of flour?

questions.explanation: Convert 15km to centimetres: 15km=1,500,000cm. Dividing by the scale: 1,500,000/25,000=60cm. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A map has a scale of 1:25,000. Two towns are actually 15km apart in real life. How far apart are they on the map, in centimetres?

questions.explanation: The ratio parts add up to 10. Apples: (2/10)x100=20%. Oranges: (3/10)x100=30%. Bananas: (5/10)x100=50%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A fruit basket has apples, oranges and bananas in the ratio 2:3:5. Express each fruit as a percentage of the total.

questions.explanation: The ratio parts add up to 10. Grants: (5/10)x100=50%. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A charity's income comes from donations, grants and events in the ratio 4:5:1. What percentage comes from grants?

questions.explanation: The highest common factor of 250 and 150 is 50. Dividing both by 50: 250/50=5, 150/50=3, giving 5:3. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A fruit punch recipe mixes orange juice and lemonade in the ratio 250ml:150ml. Simplify this ratio.

questions.explanation: The highest common factor of 360 and 240 is 120. Dividing both by 120: 360/120=3, 240/120=2, giving 3:2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A paint mix uses blue and white paint in the ratio 360ml:240ml. Simplify this ratio.

questions.explanation: Let the numbers be 2x and 3x. After adding 4 to the first: 2x+4=3x, so 4=x. The original numbers are 2x=8 and 3x=12. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Two numbers are in the ratio 2:3. If 4 is added to the first number, the new ratio becomes 1:1 (the numbers become equal). Find the original two numbers.

questions.stem: In a bag, there are 3 red balls and 7 blue balls. Express the odds of picking a red ball (red:not red) as a ratio in its simplest form.

questions.explanation: Yellow sections: 2. Not yellow (green) sections: 6. The ratio 2:6 simplifies to 1:3. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A spinner has 8 sections: 6 are green and 2 are yellow. Express the odds of landing on yellow (yellow:not yellow) as a ratio in its simplest form.

questions.stem: If 5 identical books weigh 3.5kg, how much would 8 of the same books weigh?

questions.stem: If 6 identical tiles cover 2.4m^2 of floor, how much floor would 15 of the same tiles cover?

questions.stem: Find the sum of the interior angles of a hexagon (6 sides).

questions.explanation: Using (n-2) x 180: (9-2) x 180 = 7 x 180 = 1,260 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Find the sum of the interior angles of a nonagon (9 sides).

questions.explanation: Sum of interior angles: (5-2) x 180 = 540 degrees. Since a regular pentagon has 5 equal angles: 540/5=108 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Find the size of one interior angle of a regular pentagon.

questions.stem: Find the size of one interior angle of a regular octagon.

questions.explanation: The exterior angle is 180-150=30 degrees. Since exterior angles of a polygon sum to 360, the number of sides is 360/30=12. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A regular polygon has an interior angle of 150 degrees. How many sides does it have?

questions.explanation: The exterior angle is 180-140=40 degrees. The number of sides is 360/40=9. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A regular polygon has an interior angle of 140 degrees. How many sides does it have?

questions.explanation: Angles sum to 180: 2(x+10)+(2x-20)=180, so 2x+20+2x-20=180, giving 4x=180 and x=45. The angles are (45+10)=55, 55, and (2x45-20)=70 degrees. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has two equal angles of (x+10) degrees each, and the third angle is (2x-20) degrees. Find x and all three angles.

questions.explanation: Angles sum to 180: 2(2x+5)+(x-15)=180, so 4x+10+x-15=180, giving 5x-5=180, so 5x=185 and x=37. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has two equal base angles of (2x+5) degrees each, and the top angle is (x-15) degrees. Find x.

questions.explanation: Four right angles with sides that aren't all equal (otherwise it would be a square) describes a rectangle. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has all four angles equal to 90 degrees, but its sides are not all equal. What type of quadrilateral is it?

questions.explanation: Opposite sides parallel and equal, with opposite angles equal but not 90 degrees, describes a parallelogram. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has two pairs of equal opposite angles, with opposite sides parallel and equal, but no right angles. What type of quadrilateral is it?

questions.explanation: The exterior angle at a vertex equals the sum of the two interior angles at the other two vertices: 50+65=115 degrees. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A triangle has two interior angles of 50 degrees and 65 degrees. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.

questions.explanation: The exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles: 55+80=135 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A triangle has two interior angles of 55 degrees and 80 degrees. Find the exterior angle at the third vertex.

questions.explanation: The back bearing is found by adding 180 degrees (since the result is less than 360): 070+180=250 degrees. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A ship travels on a bearing of 070 degrees. What bearing would it need to travel on to return directly back to its starting point?

questions.explanation: The back bearing is found by adding 180 degrees: 130+180=310 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A hiker walks on a bearing of 130 degrees. What bearing would they need to walk on to return to their starting point?

questions.explanation: An octagon has 8 sides and a pentagon has 5 sides. Difference: 8-5=3. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: How many more sides does an octagon have than a pentagon?

questions.explanation: A decagon has 10 sides and a hexagon has 6 sides. Difference: 10-6=4. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: How many more sides does a decagon have than a hexagon?

questions.explanation: At 3:00, the minute hand points at 12 and the hour hand points at 3. Each hour represents 30 degrees around the clock face, so the angle is 3x30=90 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: What is the angle between the hour hand and minute hand at exactly 3:00?

questions.explanation: At 9:00, the hour hand is 9x30=270 degrees from 12 going clockwise, but the smaller angle between the hands (going the other way) is 360-270=90 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: What is the angle between the hour hand and minute hand at exactly 9:00?

questions.stem: An angle of 70 degrees is bisected (cut exactly in half) by a line. What is the size of each resulting angle?

questions.stem: An angle of 118 degrees is bisected by a line. What is the size of each resulting angle?

questions.explanation: The exterior angles of a regular polygon share the total 360 degrees equally: 360/10=36 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Find the exterior angle of a regular decagon (10 sides).

questions.explanation: 360/12=30 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Find the exterior angle of a regular dodecagon (12 sides).

questions.stem: A regular polygon has an exterior angle of 24 degrees. How many sides does it have?

questions.explanation: Number of sides = 360/18=20. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A regular polygon has an exterior angle of 18 degrees. How many sides does it have?

questions.explanation: The diagonals of a rhombus always bisect each other at right angles (90 degrees). (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: In a rhombus, at what angle do the diagonals cross?

questions.explanation: Like a rhombus, the diagonals of a kite always cross at right angles (90 degrees), even though a kite's sides aren't all equal. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: In a kite, at what angle do the diagonals cross?

questions.stem: What is the angle between the hour hand and minute hand at 4:30?

questions.stem: What is the angle between the hour hand and minute hand at 7:15?

questions.explanation: The triangle's third angle: 180-48-65=67 degrees. Since z is on a straight line with this angle: z=180-67=113 degrees. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A triangle has angles of 48 and 65 degrees. Its third angle lies on a straight line together with an angle labelled z. Find z.

questions.stem: A triangle has angles of 55 and 72 degrees. Its third angle lies on a straight line together with an angle labelled w. Find w.

questions.explanation: Using n(n-3)/2 with n=6: 6x3/2=9 diagonals. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: How many diagonals does a hexagon (6 sides) have? Use the formula n(n-3)/2.

questions.explanation: Using n(n-3)/2 with n=8: 8x5/2=20 diagonals. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: How many diagonals does an octagon (8 sides) have?

questions.explanation: Angles around a point sum to 360: 4x+2x+90=360, so 6x+90=360, giving 6x=270 and x=45. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Three angles around a point are (4x) degrees, (2x) degrees, and 90 degrees. Find x.

questions.explanation: Angles around a point sum to 360: 5x+3x+120=360, so 8x=240 and x=30. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Three angles around a point are (5x) degrees, (3x) degrees, and 120 degrees. Find x.

questions.explanation: The angle turned is the difference between the two bearings: 150-60=90 degrees. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: A plane flies on a bearing of 060 degrees and then changes direction to fly on a bearing of 150 degrees. Through what angle did the plane turn?

questions.explanation: The angle turned is the difference between the two bearings: 200-80=120 degrees. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: A hiker walks on a bearing of 080 degrees and then changes direction to walk on a bearing of 200 degrees. Through what angle did the hiker turn?

questions.explanation: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. The numbers appearing in both lists are 1, 2, 3 and 6. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: List all the common factors of 18 and 24.

questions.explanation: Factors of 20: 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. The common factors are 1, 2, 5 and 10 - that's 4 in total. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: How many common factors do 20 and 30 have?

questions.explanation: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36... Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36... The common multiples, in order, are 12, 24 and 36. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: List the first three common multiples of 4 and 6.

questions.explanation: The lowest common multiple of 5 and 8 is 40. Common multiples occur every 40: 40, 80, 120... The 2nd common multiple is 80. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: What is the 2nd common multiple of 5 and 8?

questions.explanation: Breaking 72 down repeatedly: 72=2x36=2x2x18=2x2x2x9=2x2x2x3x3. All the factors used (2, 2, 2, 3, 3) are prime. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Use a factor tree to write 72 as a product of prime factors.

questions.explanation: Breaking 90 down repeatedly: 90=2x45=2x3x15=2x3x3x5. All the factors used are prime. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Use a factor tree to write 90 as a product of prime factors.

questions.stem: For two numbers, HCF x LCM = the product of the two numbers. If two numbers are 12 and 18, and their HCF is 6, find their LCM.

questions.explanation: Using the rule: LCM = (15x20)/5 = 300/5=60. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Two numbers are 15 and 20. Their HCF is 5. Using the rule HCF x LCM = product of the numbers, find their LCM.

questions.explanation: The factors of 100 are 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50, 100 - that's 9 factors in total. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: How many factors does 100 have?

questions.explanation: The factors of 144 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 9, 12, 16, 18, 24, 36, 48, 72, 144 - that's 15 factors in total. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: How many factors does 144 have?

questions.explanation: Checking each number between 40 and 60 for factors other than 1 and itself: 41, 43, 47, 53 and 59 are prime. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: List all the prime numbers between 40 and 60.

questions.explanation: The primes between 20 and 40 are 23, 29, 31 and 37 - that's 4 in total. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: How many prime numbers are there between 20 and 40?

questions.stem: Twin primes are pairs of prime numbers that differ by 2 (for example, 3 and 5). Find the smallest pair of twin primes greater than 10.

questions.explanation: 17 and 19 are both prime and differ by 2, making them twin primes. The other pairs either aren't both prime or don't differ by exactly 2. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Which of these pairs are twin primes (prime numbers differing by exactly 2)?

questions.explanation: Factors of 15: 1, 3, 5, 15. Factors of 28: 1, 2, 4, 7, 14, 28. The only common factor is 1, so 15 and 28 are coprime. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Are 15 and 28 coprime (do they have a highest common factor of 1)?

questions.explanation: Factors of 12: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12. Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Their highest common factor is 6, not 1, so they are not coprime. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Are 12 and 18 coprime?

questions.explanation: The lowest common multiple of 6 and 8 is 24. The only multiple of 24 that is less than 50 is 24 itself (the next one, 48, would also work - but 24 is the smallest). (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Find a number that is a multiple of both 6 and 8, and is less than 50.

questions.explanation: The lowest common multiple of 9 and 12 is 36, which falls between 30 and 40. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Find a number that is a multiple of both 9 and 12, and is between 30 and 40.

questions.explanation: The lights next flash together after a time that is a multiple of both 15 and 20, which is their lowest common multiple: 60 seconds. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Two flashing lights start flashing together. Light A flashes every 15 seconds, Light B flashes every 20 seconds. After how many seconds will they next flash together?

questions.explanation: The buses next leave together after the lowest common multiple of 18 and 24, which is 72 minutes. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Two buses leave a station together. Bus A leaves every 18 minutes, Bus B leaves every 24 minutes. After how many minutes will they next leave together?

questions.explanation: Working through pairs that multiply to give 36: 1x36, 2x18, 3x12, 4x9, 6x6. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: List all the factor pairs of 36.

questions.explanation: The factors of 48 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 16, 24, 48 - that's 10 factors, forming 5 factor pairs (1x48, 2x24, 3x16, 4x12, 6x8). (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: How many factor pairs does 48 have?

questions.stem: Find the HCF of 12, 18 and 24.

questions.stem: Find the HCF of 16, 24 and 40.

questions.stem: Is 91 a prime number or a composite number? Show your working.

questions.stem: Is 97 a prime number or a composite number?

questions.stem: Is 4,320 divisible by 2, 3 and 5? Check each and explain.

questions.explanation: Divisible by 2: it ends in 5, which is odd, so no. Divisible by 3: the digit sum 2+1+4+5=12 is divisible by 3, so yes. Divisible by 5: it ends in 5, so yes. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)

options.text: Not divisible by any of them

questions.stem: Work out 6 squared (6^2).

questions.explanation: (-9) x (-9) = 81. A common mistake is assuming a negative number squared stays negative, giving -81. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Work out (-9) squared.

questions.explanation: 7 squared is 49 and 8 squared is 64. Since 50 is between 49 and 64, the square root of 50 lies between 7 and 8. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: The square root of 50 lies between which two consecutive whole numbers?

questions.explanation: 9 squared is 81 and 10 squared is 100. Since 90 is between 81 and 100, the square root of 90 lies between 9 and 10. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)

questions.explanation: 10^4 means 10 x 10 x 10 x 10 = 10,000. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Work out 10 to the power of 4 (10^4).

questions.explanation: 3 squared = 9. 4 cubed = 64. Adding: 9+64=73. (Exam boards: GL Assessment, CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Work out 3 squared plus 4 cubed.

questions.explanation: 5 squared = 25. 2 cubed = 8. Subtracting: 25-8=17. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Work out 5 squared minus 2 cubed.

questions.explanation: 2^5=2x2x2x2x2=32. 5 squared=25. Since 32 is greater than 25, 2 to the power of 5 is bigger. (Exam boards: CEM-style, ISEB Common Pre-Test, Independent School Papers.)
questions.stem: Which is bigger: 2 to the power of 5, or 5 squared?

questions.explanation: 3 cubed = 3x3x3=27. 4 squared = 4x4=16. Since 27 is greater than 16, 3 cubed is bigger. A common mistake is assuming the larger base number always gives the larger result. (Exam boards: GL Assessment.)
questions.stem: Which is bigger: 3 cubed, or 4 squared?

questions.stem: Which number is larger: 4,562,000 or 4,526,000?

questions.stem: Work out 67.2 divided by 1,000.
